in_hebrew.name: חוקס
in_hebrew.long_meaning: From the Hebrew word 'chuk', meaning 'statute', 'decree', 'commandment', 'law', or 'instruction'. 'Hux' may be derived from the Hebrew word 'hakah' meaning 'to rejoice' or 'to be joyful'. Thus, 'Hux' could mean 'Joy from the commandment' or 'Rejoicing in the law'.

in_greek.name: Ὑγξός
in_greek.long_meaning: From the Greek word 'hugxos', which is derived from 'hagos', meaning 'rejoice' or 'be joyful'. Thus, 'Hux' in Greek would mean 'Joyful one' or 'Joyous one'.

in_latin.name: Hux
in_latin.long_meaning: Derived from the Hebrew word 'chuk' or the Greek word 'hugxos', both meaning 'rejoice' or 'be joyful'. Thus, 'Hux' in Latin would mean 'Joy' or 'Rejoicing'.
